title: Mouse Kaomoji ᘛ⁐̤ᕐᐷ: Copy & Paste Mouse and Hamster Faces
meta_description: Copy mouse kaomoji and hamster text faces: the side-on ᘛ⁐̤ᕐᐷ mouse, <:3 )~ with a long tail, ~~(__^·> scurrying mice and round ₍ᐢ•ﻌ•ᐢ₎ hamsters to paste.
hero_tagline: Mice, rats and hamsters drawn in text, from tiny tailed mice to chubby hamster cheeks. Tap one to copy.
intro: Text mice are usually drawn from the side. In ᘛ⁐̤ᕐᐷ the ᘛ at the left is the curl of the tail, ⁐ with two dots underneath is the body and little feet, ᕐ is a round ear and ᐷ is the pointed nose. The keyboard version <:3 )~ turns the same idea around: < is the snout, :3 is the eye and whiskered mouth, and ~ is the tail trailing behind. Hamsters are drawn face-on instead, with ᐢ ears and puffed cheeks. The syllabics mice need a font for Canadian Aboriginal syllabics, so a few older devices show boxes; the punctuation mice work everywhere. Picture versions, 🐭 🐁 🐀 🐹, are on the animal emoji page.

sections.intro: Typed with ordinary keys. The ~ tail gets longer the more you add.

sections.label: Mouse Faces
sections.intro: Round ears on each side and whiskers made of = signs or a ᴥ snout.

sections.label: Hamsters
sections.intro: Hamsters get small ᐢ ears and the ₍ ₎ brackets read as full cheek pouches.

faq.a: It is a mouse seen from the side: < is the pointed nose, :3 is the eye and whiskery mouth, ) is the body and ~ is the tail. It is one of the oldest Western text mice and uses only keyboard characters.

ᘛ, ᕐ and ᐷ are Canadian Aboriginal syllabics, and ⁐ is the close-up punctuation mark U+2050 with a combining diaeresis below it for the feet. If any one of them is missing from the reader's font, the mouse shows as a box.
Yes. ₍ᐢ•ﻌ•ᐢ₎ is the common one: ᐢ are the small rounded ears and the subscript brackets ₍ ₎ make the face look wide, like cheeks full of food.
